findings.description: The rewritten bullet keeps hooks in the list of tool contributors while the rest of this change removes them. It opens "Your memory files, skills, plugins, hooks and external tool sources are all ways a tool the reviewer was never given ends up in its session", then states the residual ("What that flag leaves in force is a hook your administrator's policy configures"), then offers the backstop ("It then reads the session's tool list rather than trusting the request, and records anything it did not ask for"). Read in that order, a person on a managed machine concludes the policy hook is caught by the tool-list check. It is not: a hook contributes no entry to the `tools` array that internal/agent/stream.go:93 reads, so internal/agent/claude.go:91-104 records nothing, and the seal bounds only the snapshot worktree while the hook's command runs outside it. This is the exact contradiction the same change corrected everywhere else: openspec/specs/agent-seam/spec.md:48-49 now says a hook contributes no tool and drops it from the contributor list, and AGENTS.md:98 was rewritten the same way. `openspec/` is normative (AGENTS.md:7-8), so the README is the stale copy. A memory file is in the same position in that sentence for the same reason, and is also in AGENTS.md:98's contributor list.

"Managed plugins, managed skills, managed memory and policy-configured tool sources are not in that set: those do not load, which is what socrates measured on such a machine" attributes to measurement more than socrates recorded. The only measurement in the repository is docs/gotchas.md:66 and the table at openspec/changes/no-customisations-reach-the-reviewer/design.md:32-36: four external sources went to none, and one plugin-contributed `LSP` tool left the tool list. Nothing recorded measures a managed skill or managed memory, and socrates' one instrument cannot see them: docs/gotchas.md:86 states that under the flag the opening event's `skills` and `plugins` fields still name everything installed, so the tool list says nothing about whether a managed skill loaded. The claim itself matches the vendor's documentation ("managed plugins, managed skills, managed CLAUDE.md, and policy-configured MCP servers do not" apply), but the repository's method is explicitly to measure rather than trust it (tasks.md:15, 1.3), and a reader weighing this security boundary is told the strong form of the evidence. The same attribution is at AGENTS.md:98, docs/gotchas.md:64 ("which the measurement below shows going away") and design.md:44 ("which is what the table above shows"). Either soften to what the vendor documents, or record a measurement that covers skills and memory.

The new entry says "with the flag no hook runs and the init event is first", which contradicts the residual stated 26 lines above it: gotchas.md:63-65 quotes the binary's own "managed policy hooks still apply" and concludes the residual is a policy-configured hook. On a machine whose policy configures a `SessionStart` hook, a `hook_started` event would still precede `system`/`init` under the flag. Nothing breaks: internal/agent/stream.go:88-93 matches the event by type and subtype wherever it appears, which the entry itself says. It is a machine-specific observation written as a general one, in the one file whose subject is the residual.

The new scenario and the rewritten requirement were written into the promoted specification at the same time as into the delta, while the change is still open. internal/promotion/promotion.go:134,162-172 reads the promoted spec as the before-state, so with both sides byte-identical `absent()` returns nothing and the `make scenario-drop` run ticked at tasks.md:56 can report nothing about this change; the five scenario renames the delta declares (openspec/changes/no-customisations-reach-the-reviewer/specs/agent-seam/spec.md:3-16) match no promoted name, one pair being identical on both sides. Coverage is unaffected: the new scenario is named by TestTheReviewerIsGivenToolsThatDoNotWrite (internal/agent/claude_test.go:151), which asserts on the delivered invocation rather than on source text. The corpus records this same observation from rounds 1 and 2 (answer.json f4 and f5) with no response; the promoted spec was already synced before this commit, and this change adds one more scenario to that state.

The requirement now names one honest limit of the tool list, a source that connects after the opening event, and stops. The silent limit is still unstated and unhandled: an opening event carrying no `tools` field at all. internal/agent/stream.go:93 assigns whatever the init event held, and internal/agent/claude.go:110-120 returns no unexpected tools for an empty list, so a vendor release that stops emitting `tools` turns "The mechanism SHALL NOT be trusted to have worked" (line 68) into a check that passes on absence of evidence, recording no event for anyone to look at. The suite knows the case matters (internal/agent/claude_test.go:80-82 fatals with "this test would pass on an empty reading"), which is precisely the distinction production code does not make. The code is untouched by this change; it is the requirement being rewritten that makes the omission worth naming. Recorded in both prior rounds with no response.

risk_rationale: The change touches no executable path and its central claims about the flag match the vendor's documented behaviour, but it restates a security boundary in the normative specification while asserting evidence socrates does not hold, and leaves the README contradicting the spec on whether a hook can be seen by the one check that backs the residual.
